svg.title: The spread of each layer's output over the batch, and the gradient arriving at it: 20 relu layers as nn.Linear starts them

g.title: Forward, layer 1: its outputs differ from one digit to the next by 0.257 (the spread over the batch)
Layer 10: 5.31e-5, x0.41 a layer from layer 5
Layer 15: 5.92e-7, x0.41 a layer from layer 10
Layer 19: 3.25e-8. Every digit gives the last layers almost the same output: x0.41 a layer, 18 times
Backward, from the loss: the gradient arriving at layer 19 is 0.000535
Layer 15: 1.53e-5; the gradient shrinks on the way back, as the signal did on the way in
Layer 10: 1.65e-7; the gradient shrinks on the way back, as the signal did on the way in
Layer 5: 1.59e-9; the gradient shrinks on the way back, as the signal did on the way in
Layer 1: 5.32e-11. The first layers' weights get almost no gradient, so training cannot move them
